name: Plains
description: Flat grassland with few trees - the classic starter biome and the easiest place to build, farm and find your first village.
resources: Oak wood (scattered trees, often with beehives near flowers)
Hay bales in villages (9 wheat each)
Horses and donkeys for early mounts
Village loot: beds, food, iron gear, obsidian in weapon smith chests
whyGo: Best biome to start a world: flat building space, animals everywhere and a village head start
Horse breeding and taming
Bee farming: plains trees near flowers have a 5% chance to generate with a bee nest
tips: Mark village coordinates early - they are your first bed, food and trading post.

keywords: plains biome village horses bees starter

name: Desert

Cactus for green dye and defensive walls
Dead bushes drop sticks
Fossils generate underground (bone blocks)
Suspicious sand in pyramids and wells for archaeology (1.20+)
mobs: Husks (80% of surface zombies - they do not burn in daylight and inflict Hunger)
structures: Desert pyramids (4 loot chests + 9 TNT trap)

Husks ignore sunlight: bring a shield at dawn.
keywords: desert biome pyramid temple loot camel husk archaeology

name: Jungle
description: Dense rainforest with giant trees, bamboo and vines. Hard to move through, but packed with resources that exist nowhere else.
resources: Jungle wood, bamboo, cocoa beans, vines and melons
Jungle temple loot and suspicious gravel (archaeology)

mobs: Standard hostile mobs under the canopy

keywords: jungle biome temple panda parrot bamboo cocoa ocelot

Red sand and red sandstone

mobs: Standard hostile mobs in caves and at night

tips: Mineshaft chest minecarts here contain gold, iron, enchanted books and name tags.

mobs: Mooshrooms only - no hostile mobs spawn naturally, ever

name: Cherry Grove
description: Pink cherry blossom forests on mountain slopes, added in 1.20. Beautiful, peaceful and the only source of cherry wood.

Pink petals (renewable ground cover, bone-mealable)

name: Deep Dark

Deepslate and the ore veins around Y=-59
mobs: The Warden (summoned by sculk shriekers - 500 HP, kills through netherite)

The ultimate stealth challenge
tips: Bring wool: walking on wool and placing wool around sensors makes you silent. Swift Sneak III changes everything.
Shriekers need 4 activations (within 10 minutes) to summon a Warden - break them after every mistake instead of running.
keywords: deep dark biome ancient city warden sculk shrieker swift sneak

mobs: Slimes at night (light below 8, Y 51-69, moon-dependent)
Witches in huts; bogged (poison-arrow skeletons) in swamps and mangroves (1.21)

Frogs for froglights (feed them small magma cubes)
Mud and mangrove wood palettes from the mangrove variant
tips: Slime rates are zero at new moon - check the moon before an AFK session.
Witch huts make compact witch farms (redstone, glowstone, gunpowder) with a small spawn volume.

Sweet berries (food and fox bait)
Podzol (grows mushrooms at any light)
Mossy cobblestone boulders
mobs: Foxes (trust players who sneak-feed them sweet berries)

Exposed coal and iron ore on cliff faces
Infested stone (silverfish) below Y=0 - mine carefully
Goats on jagged and frozen peaks (ram horns, 1.19+)

description: Dense oak and birch woodland - the classic tree farm biome with flowers, wolves and the occasional beehive.

Wolves (tame them for skeleton protection)

name: Savanna

Village loot and easy trading (savanna villages are common)
Llamas for caravan storage

Horses

name: Ice Spikes

Snow and regular ice

name: Mangrove Swamp

Moss carpets
mobs: Frogs, tropical fish in warm water
Slimes at night in swamp chunks
structures: No exclusive structures; witch huts do not generate here (that is the temperate swamp)

keywords: mangrove swamp mud bricks frogs white warm clay propagule

name: Lush Caves
description: Glowing underground gardens of moss, clay pools, glow berries and axolotls - marked on the surface by azalea trees.
resources: Axolotls (blue one is a 1/1200 breeding chance)
Glow berries (food + light)
Moss blocks, azalea, flowering azalea, spore blossoms
Clay in pools
Dripleaf for parkour and farms
Tropical fish
mobs: Axolotls, glow squid, tropical fish, bats

Bucket every axolotl color - they breed with tropical fish buckets.

keywords: lush caves axolotl glow berries azalea moss spore blossom clay

name: Dripstone Caves
description: Vast caverns of dripstone spikes and pillars, with copper-rich ore veins and water pools guarded by drowned.
resources: Pointed dripstone (renewable: grows under dripstone blocks with water/lava above)

Dripstone blocks for decoration and lava farms
Drowned (trident source in aquifers)

whyGo: The best copper mining in the game, plus infinite lava farms: pointed dripstone dripping lava into cauldrons fills them slowly but forever.

Pair with a nearby lush cave for a complete underground resource loop.

name: Nether Wastes
description: The classic netherrack expanse - zombified piglins, ghasts and lava seas, with striders riding the lava lakes.

Zombified piglin gold farms (nuggets and ingots)
Striders for lava travel (saddle + warped fungus on a stick)
Ghast tears
whyGo: The backbone Nether biome: quartz for XP and redstone parts, the classic zombified piglin gold farm location, and fortress hunting grounds.

name: Crimson Forest
description: A red fungal forest of huge crimson fungi, shroomlights and weeping vines, crawling with piglins and hoglins.

Piglin bartering (gold for pearls, obsidian, potions...)
Weeping vines and crimson nylium

whyGo: Piglin bartering halls work best here, hoglin farms supply infinite food, and crimson stems are a striking fireproof building wood.
tips: Wear one gold armor piece and piglins stay neutral.
Hoglins avoid warped fungus - carry some as a repellent shield.
Hoglins zombify in the Overworld, so farm them in the Nether.
keywords: crimson forest piglin hoglin bartering shroomlight nylium stems bastion

name: Warped Forest
description: A cyan-blue fungal forest filled with endermen - the calmest and safest Nether biome, with no ghasts and no piglins.
resources: Warped stems (fire-proof blue wood) and shroomlights
Ender pearls from the dense enderman spawns - the best early pearl farm
Warped fungus on a stick crafting for strider riding
Twisting vines
structures: Bastion remnants and ruined portals can appear; no fortresses exclusive

Looting III sword turns one visit into stacks of pearls.

name: Soul Sand Valley
description: A foggy canyon of soul sand and soul soil, basalt pillars and ancient fossils - slow to cross, rich in bone and ghast tears.

structures: Bastions and ruined portals can generate

name: The End

End stone and purpur blocks

name: Meadow

Oak and birch mixed in - but no bee nests on these trees

Vindicators and evokers if a woodland mansion generates inside

name: Flower Forest

resources: Nearly every flower: tulips, cornflowers, lilies of the valley, alliums, poppies, dandelions and more - a dye supermarket

mobs: Rabbits (instead of the wolves of regular forests)
Bees around the many nests - pollinating the flower carpet
Standard farm animals and hostile mobs at night

Rabbit farming for rabbit's feet (jump boost potions)

Dolphins - feed them raw fish and they lead you to ruins or shipwrecks

Treasure maps from the ruins, dolphin-guided

description: The signature 1.18 mountain summit: bare stone peaks under a layer of snow blocks, with jagged ridgelines that can reach the world height limit of Y 256.
resources: Emerald ore - mountains are the only Overworld biome type that generates it, and veins get more common with altitude
Infested stone (silverfish) hiding among the regular stone
Coal and iron ore exposed on the cliff faces
Snow and snow blocks in bulk
Goats - only mountain biomes spawn them
mobs: Goats (mountain biomes only) - they drop goat horns when they ram solid blocks
Standard hostile mobs at night; in Bedrock, strays replace skeletons under open sky
structures: Ruined portals occasionally on the slopes
whyGo: Emerald hunting: strip the upper peak, where emerald ore generates most often - no other Overworld biome has it.
Goat horns: trick a goat into ramming a tree or stone block.
Snow farms and some of the best building scenery in the game, often ringing a meadow or cherry grove valley.
tips: Steep drops are the real killer here - carry a water bucket or elytra.
Silverfish infest the stone: mine suspect blocks with care or a Silk Touch pickaxe (infested stone breaks instantly with anything).
The summit is not the powder snow trap zone - that is snowy slopes and groves - but watch the white edges anyway.
keywords: jagged peaks minecraft biome emerald ore mountain goat horn snow pillager outpost silverfish

name: Frozen Peaks
description: The icy sibling of jagged peaks: the same dramatic summit shapes, but the mountain is made of ice and packed ice under the snow - only in the coldest mountain ranges.
resources: Packed ice and regular ice in huge amounts - the whole summit is ice
Snow and snow blocks
Emerald ore and infested stone, like every mountain biome
Goats
mobs: Standard hostile mobs at night; in Bedrock, strays replace skeletons under open sky
whyGo: Packed ice for boat highways and farms: skip the rare ice spikes and mine an entire frozen summit instead (packed ice never melts).
Emeralds at altitude plus goat horns, with the coldest-zone scenery.
Blue ice crafting: 9 packed ice per block, the fastest boat surface in the game.
tips: Silk Touch is required to harvest ice and packed ice blocks.
Ice is slippery and the cliffs are lethal - boots on, bucket out.
If your summit is bare stone instead of ice, you are on jagged peaks; frozen peaks only generate in colder temperature zones.
keywords: frozen peaks minecraft biome packed ice blue ice emerald ore mountain goat silk touch

name: Grove
description: A snowy spruce forest wrapped around mountain slopes: snow blocks underfoot, patches of powder snow, and the home of snow foxes and snowy wolves just below the peaks.
resources: Spruce and pine wood
Powder snow - scoop it with a bucket
Snow blocks
Emerald ore and infested stone underground, like every mountain biome
mobs: Standard hostile mobs at night; strays under open sky in Bedrock
whyGo: Tame a snowy wolf or befriend a snow fox with sweet berries.
Powder snow for traps and farms without climbing to the summits.
Spruce wood on a scenic slope, one tier below the emerald-rich jagged and frozen peaks.
tips: Powder snow blends in with normal snow: wear leather boots to walk on top, or you sink and start freezing.
Bring bones for wolves and sweet berries for foxes.
Always look up - groves usually sit just below jagged or frozen peaks, so emeralds are a short climb away.
keywords: grove minecraft biome snowy wolf snow fox powder snow spruce mountain slope

name: Birch Forest
description: A calm woodland of pure birch trees - no oaks, no wolves - carpeted with wildflower patches, rose bushes, lilacs, peonies and lilies of the valley. Easy wood, easy dyes, and lush caves often hiding underneath thanks to the biome's high humidity.
resources: Birch logs in bulk: dense trees, uniform height, fast chopping
Wildflowers, lilacs, peonies, rose bushes and lilies of the valley for dyes
Bee nests on 0.2% of birches (Java) - 0.035% in Bedrock
Lush caves almost guaranteed below, with glow berries and clay
mobs: No wolves here - standard hostile mobs at night
structures: No villages or pillager outposts - rivers usually split it from old growth birch forests
whyGo: The best early-game wood farm: tall straight trunks, no branches, all the same height
Dye collection without farming: four flower types plus wildflowers in one walk
A scenic base spot with a lush cave basement already dug by the world generator
tips: Bring shears: lilac, peony and rose bushes are two blocks tall and renewable via bonemeal.
Mark any bee nest before chopping - in Java only 1 in 500 birches has one.
Dig straight down carefully: lush caves under this biome mean open caverns near the surface.
Wildflowers generate in patches here and in flower forests - stack them for bonemeal.
keywords: birch forest minecraft white trees wildflowers bee nest lush caves wood farm dye find

name: Snowy Plains
description: The classic ice plains: flat grassland buried under snow layers, dotted with igloos, spruce villages and pillager outposts. Polar bears and rabbits are the only passive mobs, and the nights belong to skeletons and strays - bring a bed and a bow.
resources: Snow and ice in unlimited quantities - silk touch or shovels
Spruce wood from the village builds and nearby snowy taigas
Rabbit hides and feet from the only passive mob food source
Igloo basements: brewing stands, cauldrons and a free zombie-villager curing setup
mobs: Polar bears (neutral - protective near cubs) and rabbits
Skeletons and strays at night; in Bedrock they are the ONLY hostile spawns here
Rare zombie horsemen; standard hostiles in Java
structures: Igloos - half of them hide a basement with a villager and a zombie villager
Snowy villages built from spruce wood
whyGo: Igloo basements teach villager curing and stock a brewing stand for free
Snow farms for snow golems and snow blocks
A flat, dramatic building canvas with frozen rivers and ice spikes nearby
tips: Snow layers stack deeper in Bedrock than Java - shovels pay off faster there.
Leather boots let you walk on powder snow patches without sinking.
Stray arrows slow you for 30 seconds: raise a shield before closing in at night.
Sugar cane uproots itself here when water freezes - check riverbanks early.
keywords: snowy plains ice plains minecraft igloo polar bear stray snow farm village find

name: Old Growth Pine Taiga
description: The mega taiga: ancient 2x2 spruce trunks shaped like arrows, rising from a floor of podzol, coarse dirt and mossy cobblestone boulders. No villages, no outposts - just ferns, sweet berries, mushrooms, black wolves, and trail ruins buried under the giants.
resources: Spruce logs by the stack: 2x2 trunks are the densest wood source in the game
Podzol and coarse dirt for mushroom farms and paths
Mossy cobblestone boulders - free mossy blocks without crafting
Sweet berries, ferns, large ferns, dead bushes and common mushrooms
mobs: Zombie villagers spawn here at the highest rate of any biome (Java)
Standard hostile mobs under the dark canopy at night
structures: Trail ruins for archaeology - brush gravel for pottery sherds and templates
whyGo: The fastest big-tree wood farm: pillar up one mega spruce and come down with stacks
Trail ruins archaeology without digging in deserts
A moody, foggy build palette: podzol, mossy cobble, giant trunks
tips: Lush caves are almost guaranteed beneath this biome - the humidity is that high.
Podzol only drops with Silk Touch; everything else turns to dirt.
Carve a spiral staircase around a 2x2 trunk instead of pillaring: safer and faster.
Snow can dust treetops above Y=200 on slopes - free 'winter' builds if you stack the terrain.
keywords: old growth pine taiga mega taiga minecraft podzol mossy cobblestone giant spruce trail ruins black wolf
